findings.title: Meaningful product/verifier change not logged in PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md
findings.suggested_fix: Add a dated entry to PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md that: (1) states what is strictly proven by the schema normalization, (2) what is only implemented/unproven (e.g., the compat alias path, any runners not yet re-proven against normalized schema), (3) what is still assumed, and (4) what would make the claim false. CLAUDE.md Document Authority Model designates PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md as canonical authority #1 (reality/failure/proof log). CLAUDE.md Anti-Overclaiming Contract requires separating code state from proof state: 'Before any conclusion, state: 1. what is strictly proven 2. what is only implemented 3. what is still assumed 4. what would make the claim false.' Neither commit 101daf9 nor the preceding canon-update commit 8c7860f adds any such entry.
findings.cited_rule: CLAUDE.md §Document Authority Model: 'PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md — reality/failure/proof log' (authority doc #1). CLAUDE.md §Anti-Overclaiming Contract: 'Separate code state, proof state, and canon/doc state. Do not collapse them.' and 'Before any conclusion, state: 1. what is strictly proven 2. what is only implemented 3. what is still assumed 4. what would make the claim false.'
findings.cited_violation: Commit 101daf9 (feat: normalize template registry schema) changes config/template_registry.json, src/pipeline_v2/service.py, scripts/xp_fidelity_test/bundle_contract.mjs, and tests/test_template_registry_schema.py without adding any entry to PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md recording proof state or distinguishing implemented-from-proven.

findings.title: Multiple meaningful slices committed together without checkpoint commits
findings.suggested_fix: Split into separate commits: (1) config/template_registry.json schema v2 data change, (2) service.py loader normalization code, (3) bundle_contract.mjs verifier helper update, (4) test_template_registry_schema.py new verifier tests. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md both state 'After any meaningful verifier, product, or canonical-doc change, stop and commit that slice before starting the next one.'
findings.cited_rule: CLAUDE.md §Commit Discipline (MANDATORY): 'After any meaningful verifier, product, or canonical-doc change, stop and commit that slice before starting the next one.' AGENTS.md §Commit Discipline (MANDATORY): 'Do not accumulate multiple implementation chunks without a checkpoint commit.'
findings.cited_violation: Commit 101daf9 bundles four distinct meaningful slices in a single commit: (a) config/template_registry.json product config restructure (+168 lines), (b) src/pipeline_v2/service.py normalizer implementation (+71 lines), (c) scripts/xp_fidelity_test/bundle_contract.mjs verifier helper (+5 lines), (d) tests/test_template_registry_schema.py new verifier (+82 lines). git show --stat HEAD confirms all four in one commit.

findings.title: Compat alias comment implies planned deletion without proof state or DEFERRED label
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comment to use the DEFERRED/PLANNED label convention and add a reference to the failure log or canonical spec tracking item. Example: '# COMPAT ALIAS (DEFERRED removal): family readers removed in Step 11 per canon spec §2.10. Tracked: FL-<N> or workbench-canonical-spec.md Step 11.' CLAUDE.md Anti-Overclaiming Contract: prefer labels PROVEN, WIRED, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, DEFERRED, PLANNED; do not collapse code state and proof state.
findings.cited_rule: CLAUDE.md §Anti-Overclaiming Contract: 'Prefer these labels: PROVEN, WIRED, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, DEFERRED, PLANNED. If something is implemented but unproven, say implemented, unproven. If something is wired but not verified, say wired, unverified. If docs and code disagree, say so explicitly.'
findings.cited_violation: src/pipeline_v2/service.py line 994 comment reads: '# Compatibility alias for the pre-normalization backend path. Step 11 will delete the remaining `family` readers after the stale authority path is removed.' This states a future deletion intention without a DEFERRED/PLANNED label and without a cross-reference to the failure log tracking entry, blurring the current implemented state with the planned future state.

residual_risks.description: The _normalize_template_registry function passes skin_family_scope and prefix_catalog through unchanged (dict shallow-copy), but adds no validation of their structure. If either top-level key is malformed, load_template_registry succeeds silently and test_template_registry_mounted_scope_is_explicit is the only guard. A corrupted prefix_catalog entry (e.g., missing preview_xp) will not be caught at load time, only at test run or runtime reference check.

The compat alias spec['family'] = filename_prefix is injected on every load but service.py still references act.get('family', '') in post-load L0/L1 reference resolution (lines 1037, 1123). If the alias is removed in Step 11 without updating those callers, the reference resolution silently breaks. No test covers the family key absence path.

testing_gaps.description: test_template_registry_actions_are_normalized asserts action['skin_family'] == 'human' for all template actions unconditionally. If a green-family action is ever added to template_sets, this assertion will fail but not for the right reason; it would also silently pass if skin_family is populated with any value when the registry is extended. The test should assert the actual expected skin_family per action rather than a universal constant.

test_templates_api_exposes_normalized_contract requires a 'client' pytest fixture that is not defined in the test file and is not imported. If the conftest.py fixture is missing or misconfigured, this test silently skips rather than fails. No test verifies that the /api/workbench/templates response includes prefix_catalog and skin_family_scope at the API level (only template_sets and one skin_family_scope field are checked).
